newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes up with WTI amid idle market.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes up with WTI amid idle market.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude markets were inactive early Monday, with gains tied to firmer West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, players said.
Most West Coast traders were out of the market to attend the National Petroleum Refiners Association (NPRA) convention in San Antonio, Texas. The gathering concludes late Tuesday.
"I figure nothing will get done until Wednesday or Thursday," one trader said.
Discounts for light grades were flat, with Alaska North Slope (ANS) last done at -$0.91 cents under WTI. An illiquid Line 63 market stood unmoved at postings plus $0.95 to $1.00.
Outright ANS prices ranged $20.19/20.39 in notional talk.
Space requests are due Wednesday for April shipments on Canada's Trans Mountain Pipe Line Co, a pipeline official said.
The line carries Canadian crudes to U.S. refiners in Washington state. Last month shipments averaged a higher-than-forecast 105,000 barrels-per-day, as low discounts for ANS attracted imports.
Two shipments of San Joaquin Valley heavy (SJV) grade sold for 20 cents under postings last.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, were steady at $14.38/14.48 a barrel Monday.
